relations.subject: eventing:advanced-keyspace-accessor
relations.evidence: Advanced Keyspace Accessors use the same bucket bindings defined in the handler as [Basic Keyspace Accessors](eventing-language-constructs.md#bucket%5Faccessors), but they expose a larger set of options and operators.

relations.subject: eventing:advanced-keyspace-accessor
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate, applied to a newly-minted object
relations.evidence: binding | string | The name of the binding that references the target bucket. For the Advanced GET operation, the binding can have an access level of read or read/write. For all other operations, the binding must have an access level of read/write.

relations.subject: eventing:advanced-keyspace-accessor
relations.object: full-document atomic counter values via INCREMENT/DECREMENT
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted; object is a literal
relations.evidence: The INCREMENT operation cannot manipulate full document counters because of limitations in the KV engine API.

relations.subject: eventing:mutatein-operation
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate, applied to a newly-minted object; qualified 'by default' per the quote
relations.evidence:
By default, a MUTATEIN operation does not modify Extended Attributes (XATTRs). To modify a document's XATTRs, you must:

* Pass `xattrs` as the third argument of your OnUpdate function.
* Pass `{ "xattrs": true }` in the `subdoc_operation_array` argument of your OnUpdate function.

relations.object: 18 to 25 times faster than reading data directly from the Data Service

relations.evidence: You can use the optional fourth parameter `{ "self_recursion": true }` to prevent the suppression of recursive source bucket mutations and to process the mutations that you have just created. If you do not add `{ "self_recursion": true }` to your operation, all source bucket mutations are suppressed.

notable_absence.finding: No Enterprise/Community edition badge and no RBAC role requirement anywhere - as on every other language/API-reference page in this batch, the only access-control-shaped constraint is the binding's own access level (read vs read/write), a Function-configuration setting rather than an RBAC construct. Separately: neither this record nor the Capella twin's ever mints a dedicated concept for six of the eight named operations in the page's own table of contents (GET/INSERT/UPSERT/REPLACE/DELETE/INCREMENT/DECREMENT) - only TOUCH, MUTATEIN and LOOKUPIN got concepts, in both extractions independently. That is a corpus-granularity gap this round also does not fully close, kept coarse deliberately rather than minting six near-identical single-operation concepts for marginal registry value.

cross_product_finding: This page is the single largest instance yet of this round's recurring 'orphan version badge' finding (see eventing-language-constructs.json and eventing-Terminologies.json for the first two): the Capella twin's identical page carries FOUR bare version-availability lines with no surrounding prose - 'Couchbase Server 7.6' immediately before the TOUCH operation, 'Couchbase Server 7.6' before MUTATEIN, 'Couchbase Server 7.6.2' before LOOKUPIN, and 'Couchbase Server 7.6' before the self_recursion parameter section (confirmed at lines 392/446/532/668 of cloud/eventing/eventing-advanced-keyspace-accessors.md) - and this Server 8.0 page, which is the origin tree for that version number, has NONE of them anywhere (grepped directly, zero matches for '7.6'). A reader of the current Server 8.0 docs for TOUCH, MUTATEIN, LOOKUPIN, or the self_recursion parameter has no way to learn any of these are relatively recent (7.6/7.6.2+) additions rather than long-standing ones. Four instances on one page make this the strongest single piece of evidence in the batch that the pattern is systemic - likely an Antora version-since macro that renders in the Capella build pipeline but is being stripped, or never populated, in the current Server 8.0 build - rather than four independent editorial omissions.
